findings.statement: Products gross margin and its percentage rose in 2026 versus 2025, which the company attributes mainly to product mix and tariff refunds, partly offset by higher costs including memory.
findings.rationale: Mix helped past margins, which fits the claim, but tariff refunds were a joint driver and memory costs pushed the other way. The passage does not show that mix alone will keep lifting margins.

quotes.text: Products gross margin and gross margin percentage increased during 2026 compared to 2025 primarily due to product mix and tariff refunds, partially offset by higher costs, including memory.

findings.statement: Management states that it expects gross margins to be subject to volatility and downward pressure, which runs against the claim that hardware margins should keep expanding.
findings.rationale: This is the company's own forward-looking view, stated in general rather than for hardware only, and it points the opposite way from continued expansion.

quotes.text: As a result, the Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure.

findings.statement: The risk factors list rising component costs, pricing pressure and shifts in the mix of products and services among the factors that put downward pressure on gross margins, so mix can cut either way.
findings.rationale: The passage names mix shifts and new lower-margin products as risks, not as a reliable tailwind, and it adds supply constraints and tariffs.

quotes.text: The Company’s net sales, gross margins and results of operations are subject to volatility and downward pressure due to a variety of factors, including: industry-wide supply constraints and rising costs for key components such as advanced semiconductors, memory and storage; product pricing pressures and product pricing actions that the Company takes in response to such pressures; increased competition; the Company’s ability to effectively stimulate demand for certain of its products and services; compressed product life cycles; supply shortages; potential increases in the cost of outside manufacturing services, and developing, acquiring and delivering content for the Company’s services; the Company’s ability to manage product quality and warranty costs effectively; shifts in the mix of products and services, or in the geographic, currency or channel mix, including to the extent that regulatory changes require the Company to modify its product and service offerings; investments in new business strategies, including in artificial intelligence technologies; seasonality; changes to the Company’s licensing arrangements, whether as a result of legal proceedings, adverse regulatory developments, changes in commercial relationships or other circumstances; fluctuations in foreign exchange rates; inflation and other macroeconomic pressures; the imposition of new or increased tariffs and other trade restrictions, their overall magnitude and duration, and retaliatory actions in response; and the introduction of new products or services, including new products or services with lower profit margins.

findings.statement: Total company gross margin was 47.9% in the quarter ended 2026-09-26, after 50.1% and 49.3% in the two prior quarters, so it is not rising quarter to quarter. These are total margins, not hardware margins.
findings.rationale: The figures cover products and services combined and are single quarters affected by seasonality, so they say little about the hardware margin trend.

response.rationale: The filing shows products gross margin rose in 2026, helped by product mix. It does not support the forward claim that hardware margins should keep expanding: management expects volatility and downward pressure, the 2026 gain was partly from tariff refunds, and memory and other costs are rising.
unknowns: The passages do not give a forecast of products gross margin for the next period.
The passages do not say how much of the 2026 products margin increase came from mix versus tariff refunds.
The passages do not separate hardware from other products within the products category.
